claimed_exponent: 1/2 under the explicit hypothesis that a standard pruned accepted component has line measure O(epsilon); no unconditional exponent improvement
theorem_statement: Let C_*=2^40. If the accepted-incidence graph contains a connected subgraph of minimum degree k and line measure tau satisfying k^2>=C_*dp and k^3>=C_*d tau p^2, then some total-degree-at-most-d polynomial Q has Pr[Q=f]>=k/(800p). Consequently, if a KTZ-pruned core at local agreement epsilon has a component with tau<=Lambda epsilon, then epsilon>=sqrt(8,000,000 C_* Lambda)(d/p)^(1/2) implies Pr[Q=f]>=epsilon/160000. A separate balanced-color construction proves that a single family covering half of every accepted line may require at least p/(32epsilon) lines.
title: Component-Sensitive Line Concentration and a Sharp Global-Cover Obstruction
verified_exponent: 1/2 conditional on fixed Lambda and tau<=Lambda*epsilon; unconditional exponent remains 1/3

theorem_statement: For prime p and 101≤d<p: (i) an F_p-irreducible Z-dependent factor of weighted degree δ and Z-degree r with k≥2 absolute factors supports at most (2rδ-dr²)/k²≤δ²/(4d) degree-d graph lines; (ii) for a fixed factor, smooth ramified accepted lifts contribute normalized incidence loss at most 1/(p+1); (iii) if d≤D<2d, a primitive Z-dependent weight-D polynomial is absolutely irreducible and linear in Z, with at most D(D-d) ramified base points; and (iv) for every d≤p-2 there is a minimum-weight D=d+1 primitive, squarefree, absolutely irreducible interpolant B=XZ+H(Y), whose raw resultant X=0 is a smooth absolutely irreducible plane curve, supporting sp>D fully accepted lines with one ramified point each but no total-degree-d polynomial matching all selected labels. These assertions isolate singular lifted points as the remaining obstruction and do not improve the global soundness exponent.
title: Frobenius Purification and the Singular-Lift Bottleneck
